correctness.rationale: For arbitrary n, the first positive-branch family is exactly two stars. Every query on that family either fails to split it, leaves at most four positive hypotheses, or splits it into two star-plus-one spaces; the latter have dimension at most two by exhaustive four-category query analysis. Thus the first positive branch has dimension at most three and the entire class at most four. For n=4 opposite edges define identical functions, leaving only three distinct; for n=5 and n=6 cardinalities 10 and 15 exclude depth four. An explicit depth-three n=5 tree and an n>=7 first-query construction with a K5 negative branch and two four-spoke stars in the positive branch give matching lower bounds. These deductions prove all n; exact independent incidence-matrix recursion n=2..11 and pathwise verification of full n=5,7 witness trees from actual standalone files corroborate the boundaries.

value.rationale: The edge adjacency relation of triangular/Johnson graphs is a canonical natural graph set system; its VC complexity had been investigated in primary literature. An exact infinite-family adaptive classification is not a simple VC corollary. The structural star-plus-one lemma yields a uniform four-mistake bound independent of the number of hypotheses, identifies discontinuous sharp exceptional sizes n=2,3-4,5-6 and n>=7, and explains how adaptivity behaves in a highly symmetric dense graph family. The result has direct interpretation in online graph-neighborhood prediction and in finite stability ranks; it is not an arbitrary parameter slice or finite table without general proof.
